title: Canonical conformal limits of subcritical FK planar maps

issues.location: Sections 5 (05-kernels.tex, Theorem ker:local-kernels) and 7 (07-metric.tex, Theorems met:rigidity / met:normalizers)
issues.description: Coverage limitation, not a demonstrated error. The paper rests on two large pieces that were not refereed line by line here. The first is the exact word-resampling or ladder-density argument behind the kernel theorem: given the continuum, the discrete readouts have a conditional law that depends only on local input and factorises over disjoint buffers. The second is the Gwynne-Miller-style optimal-constant rigidity for port passages. Both conformal roundness (the germ-triviality variance argument needs conditional independence at distinct points) and metric rigidity depend on that factorisation. The parts of these sections I did check are consistent, but they amount to only part of the argument.
issues.evidence: Theorem ker:local-kernels item 2: 'For disjoint closed real buffers, the conditional joint law given C is the product of their kernels'; used in Lemma conf:germs and Prop. comp:no-concentration.

issues.location: Theorem intro:intrinsic-input (01-introduction.tex); Section 9 proof of Theorem comp:metric-graph
issues.description: The all-vertex metric identification and the fixing of the scalar alpha*lambda=1 depend entirely on the companion paper (Metric-measure limits ..., Theorem 1.1). That paper must supply GH convergence to the ordinary unit-area sphere with the same deterministic a_n and the same fixed D_h normalization. The dependency is not circular: the companion does not cite this paper. Correctness of this step is therefore conditional on the companion.

coverage:
I read Sections 1-3 in full (model, inventory encoding, contour limits, peanosphere, three-mark sphere representation) and Section 4 in full (projections, protection, local joining, skeleton lifting, homeomorphisms, protected windows, circuits, separator meshes). From Section 5 I read the local-data part through cone estimates, chord genericity and frontier overlap; in the kernel part I read the theorem statement, the density-ratio lemma, the ladder local limit and bridge lemma, the sphere-density lemma and the selected-transfer lemma. I read Section 6 for conditional transfer and the aligned-annuli proof, Section 8 (conformal) in full, and Section 9 (completion) in full. From Section 7 (metric) I read the reference inputs, the comparison definitions, chaining, transfer-dominance, near-equality, the weighted count, rigidity, the quantile lemmas and the normalizers theorem. From Section 10 (loops) I read the chord convergence, the alternating-CLE law and the canonical independence proposition, and I read Section 11 in full.

Computations I checked:
- q=2+2cos(pi g^2/2) with kappa=16/g^2 maps g in (sqrt2,2) onto q in (0,4).
- Inventory word probability ((1-b)/16)^n (2b/(1-b))^{N_F}, with 2b/(1-b)=sqrt q.
- Correlation b/(1-b) = -cos(pi g^2/4), via Sheffield's Var C=1, Var D=1-2p.
- Wedge angle theta=pi g^2/4 and d2=2/g^2; record-image dimension 2(1-d2)<1; branch exponent d1+d2>1.
- Ladder first-passage density g(t,y) and the m^3 local-limit scaling.
- Unit-area 3-insertion tilt exponent A^{4/g^2-2}, derived by disintegration.
- Flag count 4n and the degree measure 2deg(v)/(4n).
- Euler identity for ell.
- Aligned-annuli constants a, B and the beta>2 tail; label-discard counting.
- Ring bounds 64pi/u^2 and 2pi/log(u/8d); relative ring theta(m); linear-distortion inequality.
- Quarter-turn rotation invariance forces T=I.
- Root-bypass exponent xi(Q-g) with Q-g=(4-g^2)/(2g)>0.
- Re-expression shifts (area 1/v, length v^{-1/2}, metric v^{-p} with xi=g p).
- Sphere actual-height density map c(x): monotone with the correct range.
- Scalar lemma and reflection lemma.
- Density-budget energy and charge bookkeeping (beta units cancel).

Not verified line by line: the protected-word ratio proof, the finite traversal order and field-transfer propositions, local reconstruction lemmas ker:incidences / input-recovery, the Section 7 gate, saturation and compartment construction, and most of the Section 10 face-surgery and winding arguments.
main_claim: For each fixed 0<q<4, spherical FK-decorated planar maps are embedded by uniformising their flag-triangle surface and normalised by three area samples sent to 0,1,inf. They then converge jointly to the unit-area gamma-LQG sphere (q=2+2cos(pi g^2/2)) decorated by independent whole-plane nested CLE_kappa (kappa=16/g^2). The convergence covers the area measure, the distance graphs of all vertex pairs rescaled by a deterministic a_n, and the full ordered nested interface collection, and the maximum flag diameter tends to 0.
sibling_notes: The family 211 board had entries for rank2 (q=4 critical sphere), rank12 (linear clock for tree-weighted maps) and rank4 (the Metric-measure companion that this paper cites as Intrinsic-input). The rank4 entry said no_gap_found with only partial coverage of the GM-style forcing core. That matters here because this paper imports exactly that companion's GH conclusion and its a_n normalisation. I grepped the companion's directory for this paper's title and found no match, so there is no circularity. The rank4 caveat carries over as a conditional dependency, not as a found gap.
